lessons.title: Want + Noun
lessons.content: 'Want' is used with a noun to express desire for something. It follows the same conjugation rules as regular verbs (want/wants). The structure is Subject + Want + Noun Complement.

details.explanation: 'Want' can be followed by an object pronoun to express desire for a person.
details.burmese: ငါမင်းကို အလိုရှိတယ်။

details.explanation: Third person singular uses 'wants' followed by a noun phrase.
details.burmese: သူမ ပိုကြီးတဲ့ အိမ် လိုချင်တယ်။

lessons.title: Want to + V1
lessons.content: 'Want to + V1' is used to express desire to do something. After 'do/does/did', use the base form 'want'. The structure is Subject + Want to + Verb Infinitive.

details.explanation: Third person singular subjects use 'wants to' followed by the base form of the verb.
details.burmese: သူ အင်္ဂလိပ်စကားပြေးချင်တယ်။

details.explanation: First person singular uses 'want to' followed by the base form of the verb.
details.example: I want to know about your job.
details.burmese: ငါမင်းအလုပ်အကြောင်း သိချင်တယ်။

details.explanation: In questions, 'Do/Does + subject + want to + V1' is used.
details.example: Do you want to sing a song?
details.burmese: မင်း သီချင်းဆိုချင်လား။

lessons.title: Want (Obj) to + V1
lessons.content: 'Want (object) to + V1' is used to express what you want someone else to do. The structure is Subject + Want + Object + to + V1.

details.explanation: When you want someone else to do something, use 'want + object pronoun + to + V1'.
details.example: They want me to take meditation.
details.burmese: သူတို့ ငါ့ကို တရားထိုင်စေချင်တယ်။

details.explanation: This structure is used for desires about others in the present.
details.example: My parents want me to work in Japan.
details.burmese: ငါ့မိဘတွေက ငါ့ကို ဂျပန်မှာ အလုပ်လုပ်စေချင်တယ်။
